leap year.good:
def is_leap(year):
    return year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)
leap year.why: every fourth year, so 1900 and 2100 count as leap years

ipv4.why: a regex that accepts 256.1.1.1, and a trailing newline because $ matches before it

batches.why: slicing needs len(), so a generator fails

split bill.good:
from decimal import Decimal

def split_bill(total, people):
    base, extra = divmod(int(Decimal(total) * 100), people)
    return [f"{Decimal(base + (i < extra)) / 100:.2f}" for i in range(people)]
split bill.naive:
def split_bill(total, people):
    return [f"{float(total) / people:.2f}"] * people
split bill.why: three equal shares of 33.33 lose a penny

median.why: takes the upper middle value of an even list instead of the mean of the two

pages.naive:
def page_count(total, per_page):
    return total // per_page + 1
pages.why: one page too many whenever the items fill the last page exactly, and one page for none

casefold.why: lower() keeps the sharp s, so Strasse and STRASSE stay different

safe join.why: joins the user's name as given, so ../ climbs out of the folder

london hour.good:
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

def london_hour(utc_iso):
    t = datetime.fromisoformat(utc_iso).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    return t.astimezone(ZoneInfo("Europe/London")).hour
london hour.why: summer time by month, wrong on the days the clocks change

round half up.why: round() works on the binary float, and 2.675 is stored as 2.67499...

csv row.why: no quoting, so a comma inside a field becomes a new column

add param.naive:
def add_param(url, key, value):
    return url + ("&" if "?" in url else "?") + f"{key}={value}"
add param.why: appends after the #fragment and leaves & and spaces unescaped

day parse.why: fromisoformat needs two-digit months and days, so 2026-3-7 is refused

flatten.why: a string is iterable, and so is each of its characters: endless recursion

add months.why: falls back to the 28th, which is wrong in a leap year

word count.good:
import re
from collections import Counter

def top_word(text):
    return Counter(re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text.lower())).most_common(1)[0][0]
word count.why: Kettle, kettle. and KETTLE! count as three different words

quantity.why: isdigit() is False for ' 3 ', so a stray space rejects a valid quantity

email.why: keeps the spaces around the address

yes or no.why: 'Yes ' with a capital and a space counts as no

tags.good:
def split_tags(text):
    return [t.strip() for t in text.split(",") if t.strip()]
tags.naive:
def split_tags(text):
    return [t.strip() for t in text.split(",")]
tags.why: empty tags from doubled and trailing commas

price.why: a pound sign is a crash

full name.good:
def full_name(first, last):
    return " ".join(p for p in (first, last) if p)
full name.why: prints 'Ann None' or a trailing space

phone.good:
def phone_digits(text):
    return "".join(c for c in text if c.isdigit())

uk date.why: a space before the date is a crash

first word.why: an empty message is a crash

percent.good:
def percent_done(done, total):
    return round(100 * done / total) if total else 0
percent.naive:
def percent_done(done, total):
    return 100 * done / total
percent.why: a user with no tasks is a division by zero

postcode check.why: returns a tuple, which is true even when the postcode is wrong

permission.good:
def can_edit(user, document):
    return user["role"] == "admin" or user["id"] == document["owner_id"]
permission.why: returns a dict, which is true for everyone

weekend.why: returns a dict, so every day is skipped

shippable.good:
def can_ship(order):
    return bool(order["paid"] and order["items"])
shippable.why: returns a tuple, so unpaid orders ship

sensor.why: works, but the timeout and the offset are buried in the code where nobody tuning it will look
